notes: The tutorial lists no external LED; the sketch uses the Uno's built-in LED on pin 13, so no LED is in the graph.
Breadboard row letters follow the catalogue convention (top bank 't' rows a-e, bottom bank 'b' rows f-j), not the letters printed in the image. Only the column and bank matter for connectivity.
Rail hole numbers (bp.1, bp.3, bn.1, bn.7) are estimated from the image. The red wire goes to the + rail and the black wire to the - rail.

Pushbutton port mapping is assumed. Terminal 1 is the left column (col 4: 1.l top, 1.r bottom) and is wired to 5V. Terminal 2 is the right column (col 6: 2.l top, 2.r bottom) and is wired to pin 2 and the resistor. Pressing the button connects terminal 1 to terminal 2.
The Uno GND wire is shown on a GND pin in the power header. GND.1 is assumed.
The resistor is 10k ohm per the manual. It sits in bottom-bank columns 6 and 9, and the black wire from column 9 returns to the - rail.
